title: Lifting cocharacters over a complete discrete valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $\pi$ a uniformizer and $k=A/(\pi)$ its residue field. Assume the canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/(\pi^n)$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. An $A$-group scheme means a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: the multiplication, unit and inverse diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with this base in place of the field base. Write $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finite-type $A$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every homomorphism of $k$-group schemes $\lambda_0:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to H_k$, there exists a homomorphism of $A$-group schemes $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$ whose base change to $k$ equals $\lambda_0$. Reductivity of $H$ and perfection of $k$ are not required.

source.place: WANTED locally; read author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf. proof.text: Put $\mathfrak m=(\pi)$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is local and every ideal is principal. Consequently every ideal is finitely generated, so $A$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For every $n\geq1$, $\mathfrak m^n=(\pi^n)$: products of $n$ multiples of $\pi$ are multiples of $\pi^n$, and $\pi^n$ itself is such a product. Thus the quotient systems $A/\mathfrak m^n$ and $A/(\pi^n)$ are identical, including their transition maps. The assumed bijective canonical ring map is a ring isomorphism (its inverse preserves sums, products and the unit by injectivity). Hence $A$ is complete for its maximal ideal in exactly the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with residue field $k$.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), 00FM (section-Noetherian), and 0317 (definition-complete); elementary consequences of the stated definitions.

proof.text: The structure morphism $H\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally of finite presentation by the smoothness definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Since it is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Therefore it is of finite presentation by the parenthetical definition in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Together with step 1, this verifies all the base-ring and target-group hypotheses of [lem-sfb-complete-local-split-torus-hom-lift] with $R=A$ and $G=H$.

source.place: Tag 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated) and Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation); smoothness is locally of finite presentation as in Tag 02H0.

proof.text: Use rank $r=1$ in [lem-sfb-complete-local-split-torus-hom-lift]. Its source is $T=\operatorname{Spec}A[x,y]/(xy-1)$. The mutually inverse $A$-algebra maps $A[x,y]/(xy-1)\to A[z,z^{-1}]$, $x\mapsto z$, $y\mapsto z^{-1}$, and $A[z,z^{-1}]\to A[x,y]/(xy-1)$, $z\mapsto x$, $z^{-1}\mapsto y$, give an $A$-group isomorphism $\alpha:\mathbf G_{m,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. They respect comultiplication since $x,y,z$ and $z^{-1}$ are group-like, respect the counit since all map to $1$, and respect inverse since it interchanges each indicated generator pair. These formulas also hold after reduction modulo $\pi$. Set $f_0=\lambda_0\circ\alpha_k^{-1}:T_k\to H_k$. The cited lifting statement supplies a group homomorphism $f:T\to H$ with $f_k=f_0$. Define $\lambda=f\circ\alpha$. Then $\lambda_k=f_k\circ\alpha_k=\lambda_0\circ\alpha_k^{-1}\circ\alpha_k=\lambda_0$, as required. The lifting statement makes no assumption on perfection of $k$, reductivity or connectedness of $H$, or injectivity of $f_0$.
